## Overview

This chapter analyses clonal structure and clonal expansion from the contig-level TCR table built during preprocessing. Barcode-level receptor summaries are rebuilt from productive contigs, clonotypes are defined from CDR3 amino-acid sequences in a chain-aware way, and clonotype information is joined to the refined transcriptional states.

Working at contig level keeps TRA and TRB chains separate, so paired, TRB-only and TRA-only receptors can be distinguished. The same code runs on Cell Ranger `filtered_contig_annotations.csv` files. For this public dataset, V/J gene calls and UMI counts were not deposited, so V-gene-level summaries are skipped automatically.

```{r}
#| label: load-objects
#| message: false
#| warning: false

df <- readRDS("data/TCRseq_revised_clustering.rds")
vdj_contigs_list <- readRDS("data/vdj_contigs_list.rds")

stopifnot("cluster_revised" %in% colnames(df@meta.data))
Idents(df) <- "cluster_revised"

state_levels <- state_levels_all

stopifnot(setequal(state_levels, unique(as.character(df$cluster_revised))))
df$cluster_revised <- factor(df$cluster_revised, levels = state_levels)

df$cluster_revised <- factor(df$cluster_revised, levels = state_levels)

if (!"Condition" %in% colnames(df@meta.data)) {
  df$Condition <- dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^TNFR2a_", df$orig.ident) ~ "TNFR2a",
    grepl("^Ctrl_", df$orig.ident) ~ "Control",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# Basic sanity checks on VDJ input
if (!is.list(vdj_contigs_list) || length(vdj_contigs_list) == 0) {
  stop("vdj_contigs_list is empty or not a list.")
}

if (!all(vapply(vdj_contigs_list, is.data.frame, logical(1)))) {
  stop("All elements of vdj_contigs_list must be data frames.")
}
```

## Reconstruct barcode-level TRA/TRB summaries from contigs

The first step rebuilds barcode-level receptor summaries from the contig table. Productive contigs are kept, and chain-specific summaries are generated for each barcode. Where a barcode has several contigs for the same chain, the best-supported contig (highest UMI count, then read count) is chosen as the primary chain. UMI and read counts are not available for this dataset, so the first contig listed is used.

```{r}
#| label: combine-contigs
#| message: false
#| warning: false

vdj_contigs <- bind_rows(vdj_contigs_list, .id = "sample_list_name")

if (nrow(vdj_contigs) == 0) {
  stop("Combined VDJ contig table is empty.")
}

# Harmonise sample label if already present
if ("sample" %in% colnames(vdj_contigs)) {
  vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sample = ifelse(is.na(sample) | sample == "", sample_list_name, sample))
} else {
  vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sample = sample_list_name)
}

# Keep productive contigs only, if available
if ("productive" %in% colnames(vdj_contigs)) {
  vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
    dplyr::filter(productive %in% TRUE)
}

# Keep TCR chains only, if chain column exists
if ("chain" %in% colnames(vdj_contigs)) {
  vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
    dplyr::filter(chain %in% c("TRA", "TRB"))
}

# Require essential columns
required_cols <- c("barcode", "cdr3", "sample")
missing_required <- setdiff(required_cols, colnames(vdj_contigs))

if (length(missing_required) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "VDJ contig table is missing required columns:",
      paste(missing_required, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

# Map sample names to merged Seurat barcode suffixes
# sample_suffix_map is defined in R/setup.R (sample -> barcode suffix)

vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
  dplyr::left_join(sample_suffix_map, by = "sample")

if (any(is.na(vdj_contigs$suffix))) {
  missing_samples <- vdj_contigs %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.na(suffix)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(sample) %>%
    dplyr::pull(sample)

  stop(
    paste(
      "Some samples in vdj_contigs were not found in sample_suffix_map:",
      paste(missing_samples, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}

# Remove any existing merged-object suffix, then append the correct one
vdj_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    barcode_raw = barcode,
    barcode_base = sub("(_\\d+)$", "", barcode),
    barcode = paste0(barcode_base, suffix)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-barcode_base)

if (nrow(vdj_contigs) == 0) {
  stop("No contigs remain after productive/chain filtering.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: choose-primary-contigs
#| message: false
#| warning: false

has_umis <- "umis" %in% colnames(vdj_contigs)
has_reads <- "reads" %in% colnames(vdj_contigs)

ranked_contigs <- vdj_contigs %>%
  mutate(
    umis_rank = if (has_umis) umis else NA_real_,
    reads_rank = if (has_reads) reads else NA_real_
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample, barcode, chain) %>%
  arrange(desc(umis_rank), desc(reads_rank), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(chain_rank = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

primary_contigs <- ranked_contigs %>%
  filter(chain_rank == 1)

if (nrow(primary_contigs) == 0) {
  stop("No primary contigs retained after ranking.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: build-barcode-tcr-summary
#| message: false
#| warning: false

has_cdr3_nt <- "cdr3_nt" %in% colnames(primary_contigs)
has_v_gene  <- "v_gene" %in% colnames(primary_contigs)
has_j_gene  <- "j_gene" %in% colnames(primary_contigs)

barcode_tcr_summary <- primary_contigs %>%
  group_by(sample, barcode) %>%
  summarise(
    TRA_cdr3_aa = {
      x <- cdr3[chain == "TRA"]
      if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
    },
    TRB_cdr3_aa = {
      x <- cdr3[chain == "TRB"]
      if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
    },
    TRA_cdr3_nt = {
      if (!has_cdr3_nt) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- cdr3_nt[chain == "TRA"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    TRB_cdr3_nt = {
      if (!has_cdr3_nt) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- cdr3_nt[chain == "TRB"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    TRA_v_gene = {
      if (!has_v_gene) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- v_gene[chain == "TRA"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    TRB_v_gene = {
      if (!has_v_gene) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- v_gene[chain == "TRB"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    TRA_j_gene = {
      if (!has_j_gene) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- j_gene[chain == "TRA"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    TRB_j_gene = {
      if (!has_j_gene) {
        NA_character_
      } else {
        x <- j_gene[chain == "TRB"]
        if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(x, collapse = ";")
      }
    },
    n_primary_chains = n(),
    has_TRA = any(chain == "TRA"),
    has_TRB = any(chain == "TRB"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    clone_id_paired = case_when(
      !is.na(TRA_cdr3_aa) & !is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa) ~ paste(TRA_cdr3_aa, TRB_cdr3_aa, sep = " | "),
      !is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa) ~ paste("TRB_only", TRB_cdr3_aa, sep = " | "),
      !is.na(TRA_cdr3_aa) ~ paste("TRA_only", TRA_cdr3_aa, sep = " | "),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    clone_class = case_when(
      !is.na(TRA_cdr3_aa) & !is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa) ~ "Paired_TRA_TRB",
      is.na(TRA_cdr3_aa) & !is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa) ~ "TRB_only",
      !is.na(TRA_cdr3_aa) & is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa) ~ "TRA_only",
      TRUE ~ "Unresolved"
    )
  )

if (nrow(barcode_tcr_summary) == 0) {
  stop("Barcode-level TCR summary is empty.")
}
```

## Integrate reconstructed clonotypes with the Seurat object

```{r}
#| label: add-tcr-summary-to-object
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Build metadata table from Seurat object
md <- df@meta.data %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("barcode")

# Derive a sample key on the Seurat side that matches the contig-side `sample`
# First try orig.ident directly; if that fails in your data, you can swap this to another metadata field.
md <- md %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample = as.character(orig.ident))

# Check whether barcode_tcr_summary is unique by sample + barcode
dup_tcr <- barcode_tcr_summary %>%
  dplyr::count(sample, barcode, name = "n") %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1)

if (nrow(dup_tcr) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "barcode_tcr_summary is not unique by sample + barcode. ",
      "Found ", nrow(dup_tcr), " duplicated keys."
    )
  )
}

# Check whether Seurat metadata is unique by sample + barcode
dup_md <- md %>%
  dplyr::count(sample, barcode, name = "n") %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1)

if (nrow(dup_md) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Seurat metadata is not unique by sample + barcode. ",
      "Found ", nrow(dup_md), " duplicated keys."
    )
  )
}

# Join on sample + barcode, not barcode alone
md2 <- md %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    barcode_tcr_summary,
    by = c("sample", "barcode")
  )

# Restore rownames using the original unique barcode column from the Seurat object
md2 <- md2 %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames("barcode")

df@meta.data <- md2

df$clone_class <- factor(
  df$clone_class,
  levels = c("Paired_TRA_TRB", "TRB_only", "TRA_only", "Unresolved")
)

# Sanity checks after barcode join
stopifnot("clone_id_paired" %in% colnames(df@meta.data))

n_cells_total <- ncol(df)
n_cells_assigned <- sum(!is.na(df$clone_id_paired))
frac_cells_assigned <- mean(!is.na(df$clone_id_paired))

message("Cells in object: ", n_cells_total)
message("Cells with clonotype assignment: ", n_cells_assigned)
message("Fraction assigned: ", round(frac_cells_assigned, 3))

if (n_cells_assigned == 0) {
  stop("No clonotype assignments were mapped back to the Seurat object. Check sample/barcode matching.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tcr-reconstruction-summary
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of reconstructed barcode-level TCR assignments."

tcr_reconstruction_summary <- tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Cells in revised Seurat object",
    "Cells with reconstructed clonotype",
    "Cells with paired TRA/TRB",
    "Cells with TRB only",
    "Cells with TRA only"
  ),
  value = c(
    ncol(df),
    sum(!is.na(df$clone_id_paired)),
    sum(df$clone_class == "Paired_TRA_TRB", na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(df$clone_class == "TRB_only", na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(df$clone_class == "TRA_only", na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

knitr::kable(tcr_reconstruction_summary)
```

## Clonotype overview

Clone sizes were calculated from the reconstructed sequence-based clonotype identifier (clone_id_paired). Global clone size was used for overall descriptive summaries, while condition-specific clone size was recalculated within each treatment group for condition-level comparisons.

```{r}
#| label: make-clonotype-metadata
#| message: false
#| warning: false

md_tcr <- df@meta.data %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(clone_id_paired), clone_id_paired != "")

clone_size_global_df <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::count(clone_id_paired, name = "clone_size_global") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(clone_size_global))

# NOTE: clone size is counted within each mouse (orig.ident), not pooled
# across mice in a condition. The column name is kept so downstream chunks
# and chapters still work.
clone_size_condition_df <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Condition)) %>%
  dplyr::count(Condition, orig.ident, clone_id_paired, name = "clone_size_condition")

clone_size_sample_df <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::count(orig.ident, clone_id_paired, name = "clone_size_sample")

md_tcr <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::left_join(clone_size_global_df, by = "clone_id_paired") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    clone_size_condition_df,
    by = c("Condition", "orig.ident", "clone_id_paired")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    clone_size_sample_df,
    by = c("orig.ident", "clone_id_paired")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    clone_size_class_global = dplyr::case_when(
      clone_size_global == 1 ~ "Singleton",
      clone_size_global >= 2 & clone_size_global <= 4 ~ "Small (2-4)",
      clone_size_global >= 5 & clone_size_global <= 9 ~ "Medium (5-9)",
      clone_size_global >= 10 ~ "Large (>=10)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    clone_size_class_condition = dplyr::case_when(
      clone_size_condition == 1 ~ "Singleton",
      clone_size_condition >= 2 & clone_size_condition <= 4 ~ "Small (2-4)",
      clone_size_condition >= 5 & clone_size_condition <= 9 ~ "Medium (5-9)",
      clone_size_condition >= 10 ~ "Large (>=10)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

md_tcr$clone_size_class_global <- factor(
  md_tcr$clone_size_class_global,
  levels = c(
    "Singleton",
    "Small (2-4)",
    "Medium (5-9)",
    "Large (>=10)"
  )
)

md_tcr$clone_size_class_condition <- factor(
  md_tcr$clone_size_class_condition,
  levels = c(
    "Singleton",
    "Small (2-4)",
    "Medium (5-9)",
    "Large (>=10)"
  )
)

## Overall number of VDJ/TCR rearrangements by condition

vdj_condition_summary <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Condition),
    !is.na(clone_id_paired),
    clone_id_paired != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_tcr_assigned_cells = dplyr::n(),
    n_unique_rearrangements = dplyr::n_distinct(clone_id_paired),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(vdj_condition_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-vdj-rearrangements-by-condition
#| fig-cap: "Number of unique reconstructed VDJ rearrangements by condition."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot2::ggplot(
  vdj_condition_summary,
  ggplot2::aes(x = Condition, y = n_unique_rearrangements, fill = Condition)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of unique reconstructed VDJ rearrangements"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tnfr2a-vdj-rearrangements
#| fig-cap: "TNFR2a reconstructed VDJ rearrangements ranked by number of TCR-assigned cells."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-dpi: 300

tnfr2a_rearrangements <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition == "TNFR2a",
    !is.na(clone_id_paired),
    clone_id_paired != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(clone_id_paired, name = "n_cells") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    percent_cells = n_cells / sum(n_cells),
    clone_label = stringr::str_trunc(clone_id_paired, width = 55),
    label = paste0(n_cells, " cells; ", scales::percent(percent_cells, accuracy = 0.1))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(n_cells)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  tnfr2a_rearrangements,
  ggplot2::aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(clone_label, n_cells), y = n_cells)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(label = label),
    hjust = -0.05,
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Reconstructed VDJ rearrangement",
    y = "Number of TNFR2a TCR-assigned cells"
  ) +
  ggplot2::expand_limits(y = max(tnfr2a_rearrangements$n_cells) * 1.25)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tnfr2a-vdj-rearrangements
#| tbl-cap: "TNFR2a reconstructed VDJ rearrangements ranked by number of TCR-assigned cells."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

tnfr2a_rearrangements <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition == "TNFR2a",
    !is.na(clone_id_paired),
    clone_id_paired != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(clone_id_paired, name = "n_cells") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    percent_cells = n_cells / sum(n_cells)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_cells)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Rank = rank,
    `Reconstructed VDJ rearrangement` = clone_id_paired,
    `Number of TNFR2a TCR-assigned cells` = n_cells,
    `% of TNFR2a TCR-assigned cells` = percent_cells
  )

# Display table
tnfr2a_rearrangements %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    `% of TNFR2a TCR-assigned cells` =
      scales::percent(`% of TNFR2a TCR-assigned cells`, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("r", "l", "r", "r")
  )

# Save table
if (!dir.exists("tables")) {
  dir.create("tables", recursive = TRUE)
}

readr::write_csv(
  tnfr2a_rearrangements,
  file = "tables/tnfr2a_vdj_rearrangements.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tnfr2a-trb-cdr3-logo
#| fig-cap: "Sequence logo of the most common TNFR2a TRB CDR3 amino acid rearrangements, filtered to the most common CDR3 length."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-dpi: 300

library(ggseqlogo)

tnfr2a_top_trb <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Condition == "TNFR2a",
    !is.na(TRB_cdr3_aa),
    TRB_cdr3_aa != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(TRB_cdr3_aa, name = "n_cells") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cdr3_length = nchar(TRB_cdr3_aa))

common_length <- tnfr2a_top_trb %>%
  dplyr::count(cdr3_length, wt = n_cells, name = "n_cells_total") %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(n_cells_total, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::pull(cdr3_length)

tnfr2a_top_trb_logo <- tnfr2a_top_trb %>%
  dplyr::filter(cdr3_length == common_length) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(order_by = n_cells, n = 20, with_ties = FALSE)

ggseqlogo::ggseqlogo(tnfr2a_top_trb_logo$TRB_cdr3_aa, method = "bits") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Most common TNFR2a TRB CDR3 sequences",
    subtitle = paste0("Top TRB sequences with CDR3 length = ", common_length)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: add-clone-size-to-object
#| message: false
#| warning: false

df$clone_size_global <- NA_real_
df$clone_size_condition <- NA_real_
df$clone_size_class_global <- NA_character_
df$clone_size_class_condition <- NA_character_

idx <- match(md_tcr$cell, colnames(df))

df$clone_size_global[idx] <- md_tcr$clone_size_global
df$clone_size_condition[idx] <- md_tcr$clone_size_condition
df$clone_size_class_global[idx] <- as.character(md_tcr$clone_size_class_global)
df$clone_size_class_condition[idx] <- as.character(md_tcr$clone_size_class_condition)

df$clone_size_class_global <- factor(
  df$clone_size_class_global,
  levels = c("Singleton", "Small (2-4)", "Medium (5-9)", "Large (>=10)")
)

df$clone_size_class_condition <- factor(
  df$clone_size_class_condition,
  levels = c("Singleton", "Small (2-4)", "Medium (5-9)", "Large (>=10)")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: define-top-clonotypes
#| message: false
#| warning: false

n_top_clones <- 10

top_clone_ids <- clone_size_global_df %>%
  slice_max(order_by = clone_size_global, n = n_top_clones, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(clone_id_paired)

df$top_clonotype_plot <- ifelse(
  df$clone_id_paired %in% top_clone_ids,
  df$clone_id_paired,
  "Other"
)

df$top_clonotype_plot[is.na(df$top_clonotype_plot)] <- "Other"

clone_levels <- c(
  "Other",
  clone_size_global_df %>%
    filter(clone_id_paired %in% top_clone_ids) %>%
    arrange(desc(clone_size_global)) %>%
    pull(clone_id_paired)
)

df$top_clonotype_plot <- factor(df$top_clonotype_plot, levels = clone_levels)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-umap-top-clonotypes-faceted
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "UMAP embedding showing the distribution of the top 10 reconstructed clonotypes. Each panel highlights one dominant clonotype against the full cellular background."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-dpi: 300

umap_df <- as.data.frame(Embeddings(df, reduction = "umap")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("cell")

colnames(umap_df)[2:3] <- c("UMAP_1", "UMAP_2")

umap_df <- umap_df %>%
  left_join(
    df@meta.data %>%
      rownames_to_column("cell") %>%
      select(cell, clone_id_paired),
    by = "cell"
  )

plot_list <- lapply(top_clone_ids, function(cl) {
  umap_df %>%
    mutate(
      clonotype_panel = cl,
      highlight = ifelse(clone_id_paired == cl, "Highlighted", "Other")
    )
})

plot_df <- bind_rows(plot_list)

panel_levels <- clone_size_global_df %>%
  filter(clone_id_paired %in% top_clone_ids) %>%
  arrange(desc(clone_size_global)) %>%
  mutate(
    panel_label = paste0("clone ", row_number(), " (n=", clone_size_global, ")")
  )

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  left_join(
    panel_levels %>% select(clone_id_paired, panel_label),
    by = c("clonotype_panel" = "clone_id_paired")
  )

plot_df$panel_label <- factor(plot_df$panel_label, levels = panel_levels$panel_label)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = UMAP_1, y = UMAP_2)) +
  geom_point(
    data = subset(plot_df, highlight == "Other"),
    color = "grey85",
    size = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = subset(plot_df, highlight == "Highlighted"),
    size = 0.35,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel_label, ncol = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

## Cluster-specific clonal expansion by condition

Clone expansion within each transcriptional state is summarised below using clone sizes counted within individual mice. Interpretation is descriptive: cells from the same clonotype are not independent, and each condition has four mice.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cluster-condition-expanded-heatmap
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Heatmap showing the proportion of TCR-assigned cells belonging to condition-specific expanded reconstructed clonotypes within each revised state and condition."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-dpi: 300

heat_df <- df@meta.data %>%
  mutate(
    cluster = as.character(cluster_revised),
    expanded = case_when(
      !is.na(clone_size_condition) & clone_size_condition > 1 ~ "Expanded",
      !is.na(clone_size_condition) & clone_size_condition == 1 ~ "Singleton",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(expanded), !is.na(Condition), !is.na(cluster)) %>%
  dplyr::count(Condition, cluster, expanded) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = expanded, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    total = Expanded + Singleton,
    prop_expanded = ifelse(total > 0, Expanded / total, NA_real_)
  )

ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = cluster, y = Condition, fill = prop_expanded)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(prop_expanded, accuracy = 1)), size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Revised state",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Expanded\nfraction"
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## Dominant clonotypes within each revised state by condition

These plots identify the most abundant reconstructed clonotypes within each revised state and compare their representation between TNFR2a and Control.

```{r}
#| label: make-top-clones-by-cluster-condition
#| message: false
#| warning: false

n_top_cluster_clones <- 10

cluster_clone_condition_df <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(cluster_revised),
    !is.na(Condition),
    !is.na(clone_id_paired),
    clone_id_paired != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cluster = as.character(cluster_revised)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(cluster, Condition, clone_id_paired, name = "n_cells")

top_clones_by_cluster <- cluster_clone_condition_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster, clone_id_paired) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_cells_cluster_total = sum(n_cells),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(
    order_by = n_cells_cluster_total,
    n = n_top_cluster_clones,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

top_clones_cluster_condition_df <- top_clones_by_cluster %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, clone_id_paired, n_cells_cluster_total) %>%
  tidyr::expand_grid(
    Condition = sort(unique(stats::na.omit(cluster_clone_condition_df$Condition)))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    cluster_clone_condition_df,
    by = c("cluster", "Condition", "clone_id_paired")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_cells = tidyr::replace_na(n_cells, 0L)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster, Condition) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    total_tcr_cells_cluster_condition = sum(n_cells[
      clone_id_paired %in% unique(top_clones_by_cluster$clone_id_paired)
    ])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Denominator should be all TCR-assigned cells in each cluster-condition,
# not only cells from the selected top clones.
cluster_condition_denoms <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cluster_revised), !is.na(Condition)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = as.character(cluster_revised)) %>%
  dplyr::count(cluster, Condition, name = "n_tcr_cells_cluster_condition")

top_clones_cluster_condition_df <- top_clones_cluster_condition_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    cluster_condition_denoms,
    by = c("cluster", "Condition")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    prop_tcr_cells = dplyr::if_else(
      n_tcr_cells_cluster_condition > 0,
      n_cells / n_tcr_cells_cluster_condition,
      NA_real_
    ),
    clone_label = paste0(
      stringr::str_trunc(clone_id_paired, width = 42),
      " (total n=", n_cells_cluster_total, ")"
    )
  )
```

## Clonotype sharing across samples

Because clonotypes are now defined using reconstructed chain-aware sequence features rather than sample-local labels, cross-sample sharing analyses are more defensible.

```{r}
#| label: make-clonotype-overlap-matrix
#| message: false
#| warning: false

sample_clono <- md_tcr %>%
  distinct(orig.ident, clone_id_paired) %>%
  mutate(present = 1) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = clone_id_paired,
    values_from = present,
    values_fill = 0
  )

sample_mat <- as.data.frame(sample_clono)
rownames(sample_mat) <- sample_mat$orig.ident
sample_mat$orig.ident <- NULL
sample_mat <- as.matrix(sample_mat)

overlap_mat <- sample_mat %*% t(sample_mat)
```

```{r}
#| label: make-clonotype-jaccard-matrix
#| message: false
#| warning: false

sample_names <- rownames(sample_mat)
jaccard_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(sample_mat), ncol = nrow(sample_mat))
rownames(jaccard_mat) <- sample_names
colnames(jaccard_mat) <- sample_names

for (i in seq_len(nrow(sample_mat))) {
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(sample_mat))) {
    a <- sample_mat[i, ] > 0
    b <- sample_mat[j, ] > 0
    inter <- sum(a & b)
    union <- sum(a | b)
    jaccard_mat[i, j] <- ifelse(union > 0, inter / union, NA_real_)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-clonotype-jaccard-heatmap
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Heatmap showing Jaccard similarity of reconstructed clonotype repertoires between samples."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-dpi: 300

jaccard_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(jaccard_mat))
colnames(jaccard_df) <- c("Sample1", "Sample2", "Jaccard")

ggplot(jaccard_df, aes(x = Sample1, y = Sample2, fill = Jaccard)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Jaccard)), size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Jaccard") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-clonotype-overlap-heatmap
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Heatmap showing the number of shared reconstructed clonotypes between samples."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-dpi: 300

overlap_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(overlap_mat))
colnames(overlap_df) <- c("Sample1", "Sample2", "SharedClonotypes")

ggplot(overlap_df, aes(x = Sample1, y = Sample2, fill = SharedClonotypes)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = SharedClonotypes), size = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Shared\nclonotypes") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Quantifying Treg_tissue_like clonal dominance by condition

The preceding plots were produced from clone sizes pooled across mice. Because the same clonotype can be counted across animals, and because pooled counts hide mouse-to-mouse variation, clone size and dominance were recalculated separately within each mouse (@tbl-treg-clone-dominance-summary).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-treg-clone-dominance-summary
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of Treg_tissue_like clonotype expansion and dominance metrics by condition."

treg_clone_sizes <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    cluster_revised == "Treg_tissue_like",
    !is.na(Condition),
    !is.na(clone_id_paired),
    clone_id_paired != ""
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(Condition, orig.ident, clone_id_paired, name = "clone_size")

treg_clone_dominance_summary <- treg_clone_sizes %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Condition, orig.ident) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(clone_size), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    clone_rank = dplyr::row_number(),
    expanded = clone_size > 1,
    large_clone = clone_size >= 10
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_treg_tcr_cells = sum(clone_size),
    n_unique_clonotypes = dplyr::n_distinct(clone_id_paired),
    max_clone_size = max(clone_size),
    median_clone_size = stats::median(clone_size),
    mean_clone_size = mean(clone_size),
    fraction_cells_in_expanded_clones = sum(clone_size[expanded]) / sum(clone_size),
    fraction_cells_in_large_clones = sum(clone_size[large_clone]) / sum(clone_size),
    top_5_clone_fraction = sum(clone_size[clone_rank <= 5]) / sum(clone_size),
    top_10_clone_fraction = sum(clone_size[clone_rank <= 10]) / sum(clone_size),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  treg_clone_dominance_summary,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Per-mouse Treg_tissue_like clone expansion (each row is one mouse)."
)
```

@fig-treg-clone-size-distribution-condition shows the per-mouse clone-size distribution. Almost all Treg_tissue_like clonotypes are singletons in every mouse, and the largest clone contains `r max(treg_clone_dominance_summary$max_clone_size, na.rm = TRUE)` cells.

```{r}
#| label: fig-treg-clone-size-distribution-condition
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Per-mouse distribution of reconstructed clonotype sizes within Treg_tissue_like cells. Each panel is one mouse."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-dpi: 300

ggplot2::ggplot(
  treg_clone_sizes,
  ggplot2::aes(x = factor(clone_size), fill = Condition)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ orig.ident, nrow = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Number of Treg_tissue_like cells per clonotype",
    y = "Number of clonotypes (log10)",
    fill = "Condition"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-expansion-by-state-per-mouse

#| tbl-cap: "Cells in expanded clones (size >= 2 within a mouse) by revised state, summarised per mouse."

expansion_by_state <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cluster_revised), !is.na(clone_size_sample)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster_revised, orig.ident) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_cells = dplyr::n(),
    pct_expanded = 100 * mean(clone_size_sample >= 2),
    .groups = "drop"

  dplyr::group_by(cluster_revised) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_cells_with_tcr = sum(n_cells),
    mice_with_ge20_cells = sum(n_cells >= 20),
    median_pct_expanded = round(median(pct_expanded[n_cells >= 20]), 1),
    min_pct_expanded = round(min(pct_expanded[n_cells >= 20]), 1),
    max_pct_expanded = round(max(pct_expanded[n_cells >= 20]), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(median_pct_expanded))

knitr::kable(expansion_by_state)

# Global largest clones: how many mice does each one span?
top_global <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::group_by(clone_id_paired) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    size = dplyr::n(),
    n_mice = dplyr::n_distinct(orig.ident),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(size)) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10)

knitr::kable(top_global, caption = "Ten largest clonotypes overall and the number of mice each spans.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-single-chain-check
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of single-chain cells on clone definitions."

# 1. How many TCR-assigned cells are single-chain?
chain_counts <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::count(Condition, clone_class) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = clone_class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
knitr::kable(chain_counts, caption = "TCR-assigned cells by chain completeness.")

# 2. How many TRA_only cells share their alpha CDR3 with a paired clone?
paired_alpha <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(clone_class == "Paired_TRA_TRB") %>%
  dplyr::pull(TRA_cdr3_aa) %>% unique()

tra_only <- md_tcr %>% dplyr::filter(clone_class == "TRA_only")
cat("TRA_only cells:", nrow(tra_only),
    "| sharing alpha CDR3 with a paired clone:",
    sum(tra_only$TRA_cdr3_aa %in% paired_alpha), "\n")

paired_beta <- md_tcr %>%
  dplyr::filter(clone_class == "Paired_TRA_TRB") %>%
  dplyr::pull(TRB_cdr3_aa) %>% unique()

trb_only <- md_tcr %>% dplyr::filter(clone_class == "TRB_only")
cat("TRB_only cells:", nrow(trb_only),
    "| sharing beta CDR3 with a paired clone:",
    sum(trb_only$TRB_cdr3_aa %in% paired_beta), "\n")

# 3. Per-mouse % of cells in expanded clones by state: all cells vs paired only
expansion_compare <- function(dat, label) {
  dat %>%
    dplyr::add_count(orig.ident, clone_id_paired, name = "sz") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(cluster_revised, orig.ident) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), pct = 100 * mean(sz >= 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n >= 20) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(cluster_revised) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(!!label := round(median(pct), 1), .groups = "drop")
}

cmp <- dplyr::full_join(
  expansion_compare(md_tcr, "median_pct_expanded_all"),
  expansion_compare(dplyr::filter(md_tcr, clone_class == "Paired_TRA_TRB"),
                    "median_pct_expanded_paired_only"),
  by = "cluster_revised"
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median % of cells in expanded clones: all TCR cells vs fully paired cells only.")
```

## Interpretation

TCR chains were recovered for about 90% of cells, and roughly three-quarters of cells carried both a TRA and a TRB chain, so most of the dataset can be read at clonotype level.

The lung CD4⁺ repertoire is highly diverse. Most clonotypes are seen in a single cell, and almost all clonotypes are private to one mouse: only a handful are shared between animals. This is expected for polyclonal CD4⁺ T cells from unimmunised mice.

Clonal expansion is concentrated in effector states:

- **Th1/cytotoxic-like** cells hold most of the expanded cells, including nearly all clones of ten or more cells within a mouse.
- **Activated/memory-like** and **cycling** states also contain expanded clones.
- **Naive-like** and **Treg resting-like** cells are almost entirely singletons, consistent with antigen-inexperienced or homeostatic populations.

TNFR2 agonism does not focus the repertoire on a few dominant clones. TNFR2a-treated mice have more cells in large clones than controls, but these sit mainly in the Th1/cytotoxic-like and cycling states, and they come from a few mice rather than all of them, so they should not be over-interpreted.

### Interpretation of Treg_tissue_like clonal dominance

TNFR2a quadruples the size of the Treg tissue-like compartment, yet its clonal structure hardly changes:

- Almost every Treg tissue-like clonotype is a singleton in every mouse.
- The largest clone contains only a few cells.
- The fraction of Treg tissue-like cells in expanded clones is low in both arms.

The expansion is therefore **polyclonal**. TNFR2 signalling enlarges the tissue Treg pool across many clonotypes at once, instead of selecting a few antigen-specific clones. This fits a cytokine-receptor-driven mechanism better than a TCR-driven one.

## Summary

- At least one TCR chain was recovered for about 90% of cells. Clonotypes are highly diverse and almost entirely private to each mouse.
- Clonal expansion is concentrated in Th1/cytotoxic-like, activated/memory-like and cycling cells, while naive-like and resting Treg cells are almost entirely singletons.
- TNFR2 agonism expands tissue Tregs polyclonally, with no emergence of dominant Treg clones.
- Clone sizes are counted within each mouse throughout, so clonotypes shared between animals do not inflate expansion estimates.
